unit.why: A teaching quoted from Netiv Mitzvotekha on spiritual gifts frames a short anecdote: the Apta rebbe says before the congregation that he does not trust himself, then tells an aged maggid of Barnov, a disciple of the Maggid of Mezeritch, that he trusts him alone.

stories.start_quote: בנתיב מצותיך שביל אמונה שביל ה׳
stories.end_quote: שלא יסוג אחור אבל לא לאחר עכ״ל
stories.summary_en: The Apta rebbe recalls that the grasses of the field told him the future and asked God to take this gift away; once, among the God-fearing, he declared that he does not trust himself for a moment, nor the young or even the old, except for the ninety-year-old maggid of Barnov, who had served the Maggid of Mezeritch and seen a bow of fire over him at prayer.
